pipeline_name: Russian Federation – Turkey Natural Gas Main Transmission Line

validity.recommendation: Change Status mothballed -> operating (line is BOTAS West corridor still in service); StartYear1 1986 is construction start (commissioned 1987-88); StartCountryOrArea Russia -> Türkiye; Capacity 4 bcm/y unsourced; length 845 km per BOTAS. Diameter inches is correct.
validity.researcher_notes: Real (BOTAS AR 2015, Energy Ministry, BOTAS site name it: 845 km, 24-36 in, Malkoclar-Hamitabat-Ambarli-Istanbul-Izmit-Bursa-Eskisehir-Ankara, compressors Kirklareli/Ambarli/Eskisehir). Not a duplicate of Blue Stream Turkish onshore (Samsun-Ankara): BOTAS says that line JOINS the Malkoclar-Ankara line near Ahiboz. TurkStream onshore (Kiyikoy-Luleburgaz) also separate. 'Russian Federation' in the name = supply origin under the 1986 contract; the physical line is wholly in Turkey, so StartCountryOrArea=Russia is an attribution error for Malkoclar. Status: Trans-Balkan Russian supply stopped 2020-01-01 (TurkStream) but the line remains in service (Bulgaria interconnection live, exports both ways). 'mothballed' appears unsupported by any BOTAS document. Capacity 4 bcm/y: not found; Malkoclar meter 14 bcm/y.

fills.researcher_notes: No document states 4 bcm/y for this line. Found instead: Malkoclar metering station 8 -> 14 bcm/y (Energy Ministry page), import contract plateau 5-6 bcm/y, max imports 6 bcm/y reached 1993. Searched BOTAS AR 2015 table (length/diameter/date only), ministry, BOTAS page, neftegaz Trans-Balkan article. 4 bcm/y stays unsourced; candidate none.

fills.researcher_notes: Line is NOT mothballed: it is BOTAS West corridor, in service (Trans-Balkan Russian supply ended 2020 but TurkStream/Turkish domestic/reverse exports use it: Bulgartransgaz-BOTAS Strandzha/Malkoclar interconnection agreement 2024-01-26 (trend.az); Turkey->Bulgaria exports 18.8 TWh in 2024 and 16.3 TWh Jan-Oct 2025 (Argus)). Those two name the interconnection point, not the line, so they are corroboration only.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Both name-bearing sources are Turkish state (BOTAS, Energy Ministry) - not independent of each other; corroboration from Argus (2025-11: Strandzha/Malkoclar exports 16.3 TWh Jan-Oct 2025, 18.8 TWh in 2024) and trend.az (2026-01-26... actually 2024-01-26 Bulgartransgaz-BOTAS interconnection agreement) names the entry point not the line. No document calls the line mothballed or out of service.
